lesson_title: Urban Climates: Why Your City Makes Its Own Weather
hook_text: Walk barefoot from grass onto tar at 8pm. That burn on your feet is a whole exam topic.
clip_script: Why is town warmer than the farm? Stand barefoot on two surfaces on a summer evening and you already know. The grass is cool. The tar is still hot enough to hurt — hours after sunset. Cities are built out of the hot-tar kind of material. Think of a storage heater that soaks up electricity all day and gives off warmth all night. A city is exactly that: all day the dark tar, brick and concrete drink in sunshine; all night they breathe it back out. And the city cannot sweat — its rain runs down the drains instead of evaporating. That bubble of warm air over town is the urban heat island.
visual_style: Split screen: bare feet stepping from cool grass onto glowing thermal-camera tar, then a city skyline in infrared pulsing orange at night beside a cool dark farm, temperature numbers ticking upward over the CBD.
pacing: Instant hook on the burn, smooth build through the storage heater, crisp name-drop finish.
